findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body: After callers invoke the returned disposer, subsequent `"message"` events still reach the handler. Repeated attach/dispose cycles retain handlers, causing duplicate processing and memory growth. The previous implementation removed this exact listener with `socket.off("message", handler)`.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup callback
findings.body:
When a caller invokes the returned disposer, the `"message"` listener remains attached. Any subsequent message still calls the handler, and repeated attach/cleanup cycles accumulate duplicate listeners and retain handler references.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
Calling the disposer no longer removes the message handler. When a socket is reused after logout, session teardown, or privilege changes, an attacker able to send later messages can still invoke a stale handler holding prior authorization state; repeated attach/detach cycles can also accumulate handlers and amplify attacker-controlled work.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body:
Calling the returned disposer no longer unregisters the `"message"` handler. Repeated attach/dispose cycles on a long-lived socket retain handlers, causing memory growth, duplicate processing, and eventual listener-limit warnings.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
